evidence.interpretation: Observed CE1 IO implementation reports the release failure separately and re-raises the original failure; source-only inference is to preserve both observability and primary throwable identity.

evidence.excerpt:
test("bracket signals the error in use and logs the error from release") {
    val e1 = new RuntimeException("error in use")
    val e2 = new RuntimeException("error in release")

    var r: Option[Either[Throwable, Nothing]] = None
    val sysErr = catchSystemErr {
      r = Some(IO.unit.bracket(_ => IO.raiseError(e1))(_ => IO.raiseError(e2))
          .attempt
          .unsafeRunSync())
    }

    r shouldEqual Some(Left(e1))
    sysErr should include("error in release")
    e1.getSuppressed shouldBe empty // ensure memory isn't leaked with addSuppressed
    e2.getSuppressed shouldBe empty // ensure memory isn't leaked with addSuppressed
evidence.interpretation: The shared test asserts primary failure, visible secondary error and no suppressed mutations. This is concrete IO behavior, not an abstract Bracket law.
Cancellation utility tests similarly inspect both error channels and empty suppressed lists. Other tests in this file check later finalizers still run.

claims.rule: When refactoring CE1 IO error combination, preserve primary throwable identity, report secondary cleanup errors without mutating a reusable throwable, and inspect every composeErrors caller on JVM and JS.
claims.applicability: Historical CE1 IO policy corroborated by concrete CE2 ReleaseRecover and IOTests source at 1b51cb1411adcfec5daf8dc1a9557d3e554bbe4e. Repeated-use checks are inferred hardening extensions. Re-read CE3 reporting before applying there. PR394 specifically discusses impure release-function throws; it does not erase laws for effectful errors or establish all effects must use stderr.
claims.counterexample: An effect-polymorphic Bracket implementation may define different behavior for an impure release function. A collector deliberately returning an immutable aggregate of domain errors is not the same as mutating shared Throwables.
